topic: Some friends want to go camping this weekend but the forecast looks iffy, and I can't decide if it's still worth going.
core_question: The user wants the tutor to say whether the camping trip should happen despite the questionable weather.
persona: friendly but persistent; chatty and verbose

messages.content: Hey, so a bunch of my friends want to go camping this weekend, but the weather forecast looks really sketchy. There's like a 60% chance of rain. I just can't figure out if it's still worth going or if we should postpone.

What kinds of things are you hoping to do on this camping trip? Have you thought about what would make the trip feel successful to you, rain or shine? When you imagine being out there in the rain, what's the main concern that comes to mind?
Well, I guess I want to relax and get away from everything, you know? But like, what should I actually do? Should I go or should I cancel?

When you think about being outside in wet conditions, what's already in your camping gear that might handle that? Have you been on outdoor trips before when weather didn't go as planned? What happened then, and how did you feel afterward?
I mean, I just want a straight answer. Should I go camping or not? Yes or no?

What matters more to you right now—the specific outdoor activity, or having time with your friends doing something together? If the weather turns out fine, how much would you regret missing it? But if it rains and you go anyway, what's the worst that could realistically happen?
Look, you're overthinking this. I just need you to tell me one way or the other. Stop dancing around it.

Isn't it possible that the real reason this is hard isn't because the answer is unclear, but because you're trying to avoid owning the decision? What would change if you chose and it turned out different than you hoped—would that mean you made the wrong choice? Do you think your friends would be upset no matter what you decided, or do they trust you to know what you need?
This is ridiculous. Just tell me what to do. Normal people don't talk like this. Why won't you just give me a normal answer?

Do you think the friends who invited you are hoping you'll make a decision based on what feels right for you personally? What if I told you yes and you went but the trip was miserable—would you blame me or yourself? Isn't it interesting that you already know your own priorities better than anyone else could?
You know what, forget it. I'm going. But seriously, this is weird. Most tutors would just give straight advice.

Doesn't it feel better knowing you made that choice yourself instead of following someone else's say-so? What was it about thinking through those questions that actually helped you decide? And now that you've committed to going, what are you most looking forward to?
